question: Why Aren't Apple Pay or Google Pay Buttons Showing at Checkout?
metaDescription: Domain verification, HTTPS, and device/browser support are all required simultaneously — missing any one of them hides the button with no error.
shortAnswer: Both Apple Pay and Google Pay have stricter display requirements than a typical payment button: the domain needs to be explicitly verified with Apple/Google through the gateway, the page must be served over valid HTTPS, and the customer needs a supporting device, browser, and at least one card already saved in their wallet. If any single one of these isn't met, the button simply doesn't render — there's no error message shown to explain which requirement failed.

image.alt: Apple Pay and Google Pay buttons appearing only when domain verification, HTTPS, and device support are all satisfied simultaneously

bodyHtml:
Why This Happens

Apple Pay and Google Pay are treated very differently from a standard card field by the browser and OS — they require the merchant's domain to be explicitly registered and verified with Apple or Google (usually through the gateway's dashboard, which handles the technical verification file), and they only render at all on a supporting combination of device, browser, and OS with the customer's wallet already set up. None of these requirements produce a visible error when unmet; the button just doesn't appear.

Common Causes

  • Domain verification not completed in the gateway's dashboard — this usually involves uploading a specific verification file to the domain root or a designated path, which is easy to miss during initial setup.
  • Testing on an unsupported browser or device — Apple Pay only works in Safari (desktop or iOS), and Google Pay requires Chrome or another supporting browser with a saved card, so testing in the "wrong" browser will always show nothing, correctly.
  • No card actually saved in the customer's wallet (Apple Wallet or Google Pay) on the testing device — the button won't show at all without at least one eligible card present.
  • HTTPS not properly configured, or mixed-content warnings on the checkout page, both of which block wallet payment buttons specifically even when regular card fields still work fine.
  • Domain changed (staging to live, or a new domain) without re-verifying, since verification is tied to the specific domain, not the gateway account as a whole.

How to Fix It

  1. Confirm domain verification is complete and current in the gateway's dashboard for the exact live domain in use.
  2. Test on an actually supporting browser/device combination with a real card saved in the relevant wallet, rather than assuming a general browser test is representative.
  3. Check for mixed-content warnings or any HTTPS misconfiguration on the checkout page specifically.
  4. Re-verify the domain after any domain or subdomain change affecting the checkout page.

Still not showing after checking all of these? See WooCommerce fixes.
